citation: Florence Scovel Shinn, "I never saw so many mis-fit sailor hats", pen and ink drawing for "From a Steamer Chair", Century Magazine 68:160 (May 1904). Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Cabinet of American Illustration, CAI - Shinn, no. 5, LC-USZ62-82966 (item 2010717915).
author: Florence Scovel Shinn
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Cabinet of American Illustration; reference image 2a14681r.jpg read at tile.loc.gov.
locator: The whole drawing: four women standing in profile and three-quarter view, full length, each in a flat-crowned sailor hat.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication', with the Cabinet of American Illustration's note. Published 1904. Used only as a reference picture for the shape and set of a 1904 sailor hat (T-3481); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3481) from the LOC reference image. Four women on a steamer's deck in long coats, each in a flat-crowned straw sailor hat with a straight brim and a dark band round the crown, set level and a little forward on hair drawn up and back. A magazine illustration, drawn, of travellers rather than working women; read for the hat.
note: A reference picture for the 1904 parlor maid's sailor hat, Christine Nelson of the Glessner household (data/humans/recipes/errand_1904.json).
what_it_supplies: the flat crown, straight brim and dark band of a woman's sailor hat in 1904, and how it sat on drawn-up hair
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about Chicago, the Glessner household or Christine Nelson
